text: Carolee Schneemann served as a live version of this work in Site, a performance at the Judson Dance Theater in which Robert Morris wore a mask shaped like his own face and walked back and forth with 4' by 8' sheets of plywood in order to both reveal and hide the scene. text: In the third movement Toccare of one of this man's works, the orchestra plays a high A on all the off-beats as the solo instrument plays a sixteenth-note melody that runs up and down the scale. That work, his Violin Concerto, was premiered by Jorja Fleezanis of the Minnesota Orchestra. He wrote the unusually quiet fanfare Tromba Lontana a year after composing a work whose movements depict the wounded Fisher King and a dream involving his daughter and Meister Eckhart, his Harmonielehre. text: The display of this work prompted the magazine Punch to create a piece parodying it, and it inspired a poem by R.S.C. in The Knickerbocker Magazine. text: This building's window depicting Joseph is inscribed Clemens vitrearius carnotensis me fecit, the only signed example of a window from its period. text: This composer used an A-flat larghetto in 3/8 time as the second movement of the later of his two piano quartets, while a piece named "Sleigh Ride" ends his Three German Dances. text: An orchestral version of this musical piece was composed in 1990 by Marius Constant. Its three sections are respectively dedicated to Harold Bauer, Jean Marnold, and Rudolph Ganz. This piece has notably been recorded by Jean-Yves Thibaudet and Arturo Michelangeli, though its first performance was given by the composer's friend Ricardo Vinés. The second movement contains a B-flat theme resembling the tolling of bells, after opening by depicting a hanged man who utters a sigh but dies by the end. The third movement opens with three ascending notes and then features a calm section meant to depict the hiding of a dwarf who'd earlier dropped from the ceiling. Its three movements are "Le Gibet," "Ondine," and "Scarbo," all of them based upon poems by the French writer Aloysius Bertrand.
